solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A flipping rubbish home device

indicators.note: flipping turns the words for rubbish and home round so they read right to left

parts.note: rot is nonsense, rubbish
a pad is slang for one's home or flat

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about an annoying gadget around the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' looks like a mild British curse on the device, but it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An adaptor is a connecting gadget, so it is a kind of device.

clue.text: Run off with sailor's conservative daughter

parts.note: AB (able seaman) is a sailor, and the 's adds S

explanation.surface: A sailor elopes with a Tory's daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: To abscond is to flee secretly, a synonym of running off.

clue.text: A teacher upset drink over the French philosophy tutor

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the word for teacher upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: pupils address a male teacher as sir
a tot is a small measure of spirits
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A schoolteacher, upset, knocks a drink over a French colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses SIR to RIS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek thinker taught philosophy to the young Alexander the Great, making him a famous philosophy tutor.

clue.text: Line of song

definitions.meaning: a railway line or a path

explanation.surface: A line of a song.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway line is a track, and a single recorded number on an album is also a track.

clue.text: Concerning call about villain coming back again

parts.note: re means concerning, as in a letter heading
a cur is a scoundrel, a contemptible villain
to ring is to call on the phone

explanation.surface: A phone call about a criminal who keeps returning.
explanation.definitionFit: Something recurring keeps happening repeatedly, returning time after time.

clue.text: Movie company look for producer of note

parts.note: a pic is a picture, a film
lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: A film studio hunts for a notable movie producer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of note' suggests fame, but it means something that makes musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: A small flute is an instrument that produces musical notes.

clue.text: Heaps of lager that European tucks into

indicators.note: tucks into says the European letter goes inside the lager word

parts.note: Pils is a pale Pilsner lager

explanation.surface: A European drinker gets stuck into heaps of lager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucks into' reads as eating or drinking, but puts E inside PILS.
explanation.definitionFit: Piles are stacks or large amounts, the same as heaps.

clue.text: Car and taxi allowed to go around Brazilian city

indicators.note: the taxi and allowed words go around the city, enclosing it

parts.note: a cab is a taxi
to let is to allow
Rio de Janeiro is the Brazilian city

explanation.surface: A car and a taxi are permitted to drive around Rio.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabriolet is a convertible motor vehicle with a folding roof.

clue.text: Lecture singer's given in Old English

indicators.note: given in says the singer goes into the Old English abbreviation

parts.note: a singer is slang for an informer, a rat; the 's is is, a link

explanation.surface: A lecture on a singer delivered in Old English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'singer' suggests music, but in crime slang a singer is someone who informs to police, a RAT.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to deliver a formal speech, to lecture.

clue.text: A single issue brought up on a single occasion

parts.note: a single is one

indicators.note: in a down clue brought up means the word for issue is read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: to emit is to issue or give out

explanation.surface: A single matter raised just once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' looks like a noun but is the verb EMIT, which 'brought up' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-time thing happens only once, on just a single occasion.

clue.text: God saves heathens in vain attacks at the front

indicators.note: at the front picks the first letter of each of the five words

explanation.surface: A deity protects pagans from their own futile assaults.
explanation.definitionFit: Shiva is a principal Hindu deity, the destroyer.

clue.text: Price for a star to make an appearance in party?

parts.note: a celeb is a celebrity, a star
a rate is a price or fee

explanation.surface: The fee a celebrity charges to turn up at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's 'party' is a noun, but the definition is the verb: to party is to celebrate.
explanation.definitionFit: To party means to have a festive time, the verb sense of marking an occasion.

clue.text: Tourists travelling over a thousand borders

indicators.note: travelling suggests the letters moving about into a new order

parts.note: K is short for a thousand, as in kilo

explanation.surface: Tourists journey across a thousand frontiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' is a link: the K is shuffled with TOURISTS.
explanation.definitionFit: The outskirts are the outer edges of a town, its borders or fringes.

clue.text: I caught nurse beginning to insult old people

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
EN is an Enrolled Nurse

indicators.note: beginning to takes the first letter of insult

explanation.surface: Someone catches a nurse starting to insult the elderly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old people' looks like the elderly, but means an ancient tribe.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iceni were an ancient British tribe led by Boudicca, so an old people.

clue.text: Old-fashioned saw

definitions.meaning: out of date, no longer in style
went out with someone romantically, as in 'she saw him for a year'

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned saw, like a proverb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saw' looks like a noun (a tool or saying), but it is the verb sense of courting someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Passé styles look outmoded; and seeing someone romantically is going out with them.

clue.text: Criminal one guards could be thus?

definitions.text: Criminal one guards could be thus?

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters being crooked, reworked out of their order

explanation.surface: A criminal that guards are watching might be a threat.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: a criminal under guard could well be a menace.
explanation.definitionFit: A guarded criminal is likely a risky, threatening person.

clue.text: Nice lamb cooked without a sign of unevenness?

indicators.note: without means outside, so the anagram goes around the letter
cooked suggests the letters being prepared into a new arrangement

parts.note: a is taken as written

explanation.surface: Lamb cooked in Nice shows no sign of unevenness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but means outside: the anagram of NICE LAMB goes round A.
explanation.definitionFit: An imbalance is a lack of equality or proportion, so an unevenness.

clue.text: It's a job serving drinks to drunks sometimes

definitions.text: It's a job serving drinks to drunks sometimes

parts.words: It's a job serving drinks to drunks sometimes
parts.note: a description of the pub worker who pours drinks, sometimes for those already drunk

explanation.surface: Pouring drinks for drunks can be a real job.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone working behind a pub counter serves drinks, including to the occasional inebriate.

clue.text: Static noise primarily on phone?

indicators.note: primarily takes the first letter of noise

parts.note: a mobile is a mobile phone

explanation.surface: Static crackle on the phone line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Static' looks like interference on a call, but means not moving.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unable to move about is fixed in place, motionless.

clue.text: Small horse straddled by short flapper's kid

indicators.note: straddled by means the shortened flapper sits on either side of the small horse
short drops the final letter of the bird

parts.note: a tern is a seabird, a flapper of wings
wee is Scottish for small
a nag is an old horse

explanation.surface: A child perched on a pony belongs to a 1920s flapper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flapper' suggests a 1920s young woman, but here it is a seabird flapping its wings; 'short' cuts it to TER.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweenager is a child aged about ten to twelve, between childhood and the teens.

clue.text: Reprimand Mark so others will see it's been done?

definitions.meaning: to scold or tell someone off

definitions.text: Mark so others will see it's been done?
definitions.meaning: to put a check mark beside an item on a list once completed

explanation.surface: Telling someone off and marking a task as done.
explanation.definitionFit: Scolding someone is to rebuke them; and checking an item off a list marks it completed.

clue.text: Given the correct pitch, United breaks weaken back

indicators.note: breaks means the United letter splits the reversed word
back says the word for weaken is read in reverse

parts.note: to dent is to damage or weaken
U is the abbreviation for United, as in football club names

explanation.surface: A football team, given the right pitch, breaks down a weak defence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses DENT to TNED; U goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An instrument adjusted to sound right has been set to the proper musical note.

clue.text: Drop girl from East Anglian town via the phone

indicators.note: speaking via the phone means the words are heard, not written

parts.note: a miss is a girl, and Diss is a market town in Norfolk

explanation.surface: A man drops his girlfriend from Norfolk over the phone.
explanation.walkthrough: Diss is a small market town in Norfolk, East Anglia; a girl from there would be a 'Diss miss'.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop someone from a job or team is to let them go, sack them.

clue.text: Really want party to go after Conservative leader

indicators.note: to go after places the party word behind the leading letter
leader takes the opening letter of Conservative

parts.note: a rave is a big dance party

explanation.surface: A party desperate to follow the Tory leader.
explanation.definitionFit: To crave something is to long for it intensely.

clue.text: More competent president right to bring in Liberal

indicators.note: the president and right letters bring in the Liberal letter between them

parts.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln, the US president

explanation.surface: A more capable president is justified in appointing a Liberal.
explanation.definitionFit: Abler is the comparative of able, so more skilled or capable.

clue.text: One about to be involved in searches for posers?

indicators.note: to be involved in puts the one and about words inside the searches word

parts.note: quests are searches
I is the Roman numeral one
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Someone about to be in on hunts for poseurs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'posers' suggests show-offs, but means puzzling things to answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A poser is a tricky problem or puzzle, something put to someone to answer.

clue.text: Line that pool player might use in conversation

indicators.note: in conversation means the word is heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a cue is the stick for striking balls in pool

explanation.surface: A line a pool player might drop into conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Line' reads as a remark, but means a line of waiting people.
explanation.definitionFit: A queue is a row of people waiting, a line in American usage.

clue.text: President's not high-class, pinching a bum?

indicators.note: pinching means the shortened president grips the a inside
U is the abbreviation for upper-class, so not high-class drops the U

parts.note: Donald Trump is a US president; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: A vulgar president groping someone's backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not high-class' removes U (upper class) from TRUMP; A goes into TRMP. 'bum' looks like a bottom but means a vagrant.
explanation.definitionFit: A tramp and a bum are both a homeless vagrant, the latter in American English.

clue.text: They watch John opening unopened horse chestnuts

indicators.note: opening means the John word splits open the conkers word
unopened drops the first letter of the chestnuts word

parts.note: conkers are horse chestnuts, used in a British children's game
the john is slang for a toilet, a loo

explanation.surface: John cracks open unopened conkers while others watch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unopened' removes C to give ONKERS, and 'opening' puts LOO inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Onlookers are spectators, people who watch without taking part.

clue.text: Boxer starts to break ineffective defence

parts.note: Muhammad Ali was the famous boxer

indicators.note: starts to takes the first letters of break and ineffective

explanation.surface: A boxer begins to break through a weak defence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'defence' looks like guarding in the ring, but is a legal plea.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a defence claiming the accused was elsewhere at the time of a crime.

clue.text: Expect drugs to have warnings on the front

indicators.note: on the front places the warnings word ahead of the drugs

parts.note: golfers shout 'fore!' as a warning
E is ecstasy, so two Es are drugs

explanation.surface: Drugs come with warnings printed on the packet front.
explanation.definitionFit: To foresee is to anticipate or predict, the same as expecting.

clue.text: Little drinks brought round for each pair of kids?

indicators.note: brought round means the little drinks word goes round the for each word

parts.note: nips are small measures of spirits
per means for each

explanation.surface: Small drinks are passed round for each couple of children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pair of' hints at the other sense, pincers, which come in a pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Nippers is British slang for small children, so kids.
